results.output:
# Today on Hacker News

## AI/ML
The AI community is buzzing with significant developments today. **Liquid AI** unveiled their latest 8B-A1B MoE model trained on 38T tokens, showcasing continued progress in efficient model architecture. Meanwhile, **Shift** announced an ambitious initiative to clean homes for free to train future robots, highlighting the growing intersection of AI and robotics. The **Mistral AI Now Summit** notes also drew attention, offering insights from one of the industry's leading model companies. Additionally, **Tiny-vLLM** emerged as a high-performance LLM inference engine built in C++ and CUDA, demonstrating the ongoing push for optimized AI infrastructure.

## Programming
Database and systems programming discussions dominated the technical threads. **SQLite** took center stage with a compelling argument that it's "all you need for durable workflows," challenging traditional database paradigms. The **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) debate sparked intense discussion, with some questioning whether the protocol is dying. Algorithmic innovations continue with **Bijou64**, a variable-length integer encoding system, while **On Rendering Diffs** explored UI/UX patterns for displaying code differences. The community also engaged with **You can just say it**, a post from antirez that resonated with many developers.

## Hardware
The hardware enthusiasts weighed in on **Framework 12**, with many finding it difficult to justify the purchase despite its modularity. On the 3D printing front, **ColorMix** for PrusaSlicer received attention for enabling dozens of colors in prints, expanding creative possibilities for makers.

## Other
Beyond technical topics, **The dead economy theory** generated substantial discussion on economic trends. Gaming news included **Snowboard Kids 2** being fully decompiled and California passing the **Protect Our Games Act** to protect the industry. Network engineers appreciated the **free full BGP feed** announcement, providing valuable routing data for labs and enthusiasts.
